title: field-add-spec
description: INPUT of `dmtool -m <model> field add <spec.json>` — a field to add, with its full per-kind config (FEATURE-GAPS §3.4) and field-level metadata (§3.5). The simpler `field add --group --name (--kind|--typedef)` flags cover a bare field; this spec covers everything the typed builders express. The SAME shape is the input of `field modify`, where it is a PARTIAL edit of an existing field: only `group`+`name` are required, and every aspect present is applied (a `kind`/`typedef` re-types; any metadata key changes that metadata) while absent aspects are left untouched — nothing the spec carries is silently dropped. `additionalProperties:false` here is ENFORCED on input: an undeclared/typo'd key is rejected with RK_UNKNOWN_ARG, not silently ignored. Validated against the real kernel before writing. (The flags and this spec are mutually exclusive.)

group.description: the parent group's ABSOLUTE name-path, e.g. /Order (must exist)

name.description: the new field's name (unique within its group)

kind.description: STRING | NUMBER | DATE | TIME | DATETIME | DATERANGE | DATEFRAGMENT | BOOLEAN | CONFIRM | ENUM | CUSTOM (omit when `typedef` is given)

typedef.description: type the field by an existing type-definition id (wins over `kind`)

required.description: true (always required) | false (optional, default) | "ifParentPresent" (required only if the parent group is filled)

label.description: per-locale display label, { "<locale>": "<text>" }; once set, must cover every declared locale

global.description: the kernel `global` flag (relevant to partial validation)

transient.description: the kernel `transient` flag (present at runtime, not persisted)

internalDescription.description: per-locale INTERNAL description — maintenance/technical notes shown read-only to *Form modelers*, never surfaced to end users; { "<locale>": "<text>" }

externalDescription.description: per-locale EXTERNAL description — the end-user-facing hint shown beside the field in the form UI; { "<locale>": "<text>" }

requiredMessages.description: per-locale custom error text shown when this REQUIRED field is left empty, { "<locale>": "<text>" } — the 'Use Default Error Messages' deselected case; needs `required` true/"ifParentPresent", must cover every declared locale, omit to use the kernel default

minLength.description: minimum character length. seeAlso: the Length operator — the rule-level way to bound length (`operators Length`)

pattern.description: anchored regex; requires patternMessage. seeAlso: the PatternViolated/PatternMatched operators — the rule-level alternative (`operators PatternViolated`)

patternMessage.description: the error text shown when the pattern fails

suggestions.description: per-locale hint list, { "<locale>": ["…"] }; validated against the field's own pattern

maxFractionalDigits.description: the decimal scale; together they bound the fraction-digit range

min.description: minimum value (decimal as a string). seeAlso: the LessThan/GreaterThan comparison operators — rule-level bounds

values.description: ≥1 { value, labels? } — stored value + optional per-locale labels. seeAlso: FieldValueIncludedInValueList / FieldValueNotIncludedInValueList — the rule-level way to (dis)allow a value set

categories.description: named classifications; each has values[] aligned 1:1 with the enum values. seeAlso: the EnumCategory operator (`operators EnumCategory`) — reads a value's category in a rule

description.description: optional editor-level note for the category (the kernel core ignores it; preserved for the editor's Category table)

values.description: values aligned 1:1 with the enum values

invalidValueMessage.description: error text for an out-of-domain value — one text expanded across ALL declared locales (the shorthand)

errorMessages.description: per-locale invalid-value error text, { "<locale>": "<text>" } — wins over invalidValueMessage; must cover every declared locale (omit both to use the kernel default)

format.description: a both-endpoints date pattern. The A12 editor offers five presets — YYYY/YYYY, YYYY-MM-DD/YYYY-MM-DD, MM/MM, YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM, MM-DD/MM-DD — but the kernel accepts any Java date pattern (e.g. dd.MM.yyyy)
a partial-date pattern (a date that isn't a full calendar date). The A12 editor offers four presets — MM, YYYY, YYYY-MM, MM-DD — but the kernel accepts any Java date pattern (e.g. yyyy-MM)
